text:
Nate: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can we get clarity on kernel v5 timeline and how it affects batching/caching SLOs? cc @Maya @Jess

Maya: Sure. Short summary: kernel v5 target is Q3 rollout (tentative). Primary improvements are a kernel-level prefetched KV cache, reduced lock contention around the batching path, and micro-optimizations that improve short-sequence throughput. Still collecting canary data.

Jess: Thanks. How will the canary rollout work? automatic rollback on regressions?

Maya: Canary plan: 1% -> 10% -> 50% over ~2 weeks. We'll have automated rollback triggers based on latency SLO breaches and error budget. Also automatic fallback path to v4-quant when memory pressure or cache thrashing is detected.

Sam: What exact SLOs are we watching for the canary and what's the ops playbook?

Maya: SLOs for the canary: p99 generation latency < 450ms (for typical 2k token window), error rate < 0.5% (client errors excluded). Runbook (short): 1) divert traffic to latency lane / dedicated replicas, 2) increase batch timeout window temporarily, 3) scale kernel replicas + raise batch size cap, 4) rollback to v4 if p99 spikes persist > 15 minutes. I'll post the full runbook link.

Sam: Can we add an alert that pulls recent prompt-length histograms and top slow prompts for triage?

Leo: We can emit a lightweight histogram metric and a top-requests sample stream. Perf cost is minimal (~0.02% CPU). I'll add a feature flag so we can enable it for the canary only.

Jess: About caching — will prefix/KV caching be sticky per user or per route? We saw correctness issues previously with user-scoped caches.

Maya: Cache key will be route+model+prefix-hash by default. We won't do user-specific caches globally to avoid unbounded memory growth. Routes can opt-in to user-scoped caching with strict eviction controls.

Dina: From PM perspective: will routing prefer v5 for latency-sensitive tiers and v4-quant for cost-sensitive customers?

Maya: Yes. Routing policy will be tier-aware. Latency-tiered customers get prefer-v5; cost-tiered will prefer v4-quant. Customers can still pin a specific model/version in their config.

Ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary started for kernel-v5 on cluster-3 — 1% traffic.

Nate: Action items I captured: @Leo add histogram metric PR by EOD Friday; @Maya share runbook link; @VP-Eng to confirm Q3 commitment and communicate risk.

VP-Eng: Confirming Q3 target, dependent on canary perf. We'll reassess after 2 weeks of steady metrics (latency, error rate, cache hit stability).

Sam: I'll create an Ops incident runbook doc and wire the alerts into PagerDuty. Assigning to myself to own the initial alert tuning.

Maya: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/ops/kernel-v5-runbook — short checklist included (divert, scale, bump timeouts, rollback).

Jess: One more ask — can we have a post-canary regression replay job that replays the top 100 slow prompts against v5/v4 to validate regressions? @Leo can you set that up?

Leo: Yes. I'll queue a nightly replay job for 2 weeks and publish the comparison report to the canary channel.

Nate: Great thread, thanks all :thumbsup: Let’s keep the updates coming in this thread so leadership can see progress.

Maya: Will do — will post canary dashboards and the runbook link updates here as they arrive.
